summary: Review-round fixes to the deployment-mode work, three of which affect standalone installs as much as clustered ones. (1) Distributed lock keys are now namespaced by application: `infra/coordination`'s Redis locker built keys as `<prefix>:tx:<resource>`, so two apps in the suite pointed at one Redis -- the documented and recommended arrangement, since Redis is what makes either app clusterable -- shared a single key space. myseliasan's leader lease and myidsan's leader lease were literally the same key, `kopiv2:tx:lock:leader`, which meant only ONE of the two apps could hold leadership at a time: whichever lost the race silently ran none of its scheduled singletons (audit retention, rollups, reconciliation, digests) for as long as the other app kept renewing. Keys are now `<prefix>:<appName>:tx:<resource>`. (2) A node that reconnects to the SAME instance no longer withdraws its own live ownership claim: the control server's teardown path fired the disconnect hook unconditionally, but a reconnecting node replaces the connection entry first and the OLD goroutine's teardown arrives afterwards, so the claim covering a healthy, connected node was released and the heartbeat -- which reads presence from that registry -- marked it lost and alerted on it. `ControlServer.remove` and the media relay's equivalent now report whether the connection they tore down was still the current one, and only that case announces a disconnect. (3) The bootstrap migration lock's 10-minute wait now actually applies: `Lock()` bounds its wait by the locker's own `WaitTimeout` (30s by default), so the wait was decoration and a migration taking longer than 30 seconds -- exactly the case worth serializing -- made every other instance give up and proceed WITHOUT the lock, into the concurrent DDL the lock exists to prevent. `buildTransactionLocker` accepts a wait override and bootstrap passes the full 10 minutes. (4) The correlator's event observation is leader-gated in the same place the sweep is, so a follower no longer accumulates arming state it will never fire from. (5) The Deployment panel now saves when only the acknowledgment changed, not just the mode -- an install already declared clustered could not record a fresh acknowledgment, so when the caveats changed under an operator, the one action the screen asked for was the one it refused to accept. (6) Event-bus topics are namespaced by application for the same reason and in the same shape (`<prefix>:<appName>:bus:<topic>`): `infra/eventbus` keyed topics by `KeyPrefix` alone, and its own comment claimed that let several apps share one Redis -- but every app in the suite is configured with the SAME prefix, so it did not. No collision exists today, because myseliasan is the only caller; this closes it before a second app picks a topic name in common and one app's events start arriving at the other's subscribers, silently.
compatibility: The lock-key change alters key names in Redis on upgrade. Existing keys are leases with a TTL and are never read after the rename, so they simply expire; no migration or manual cleanup is required. Operators who monitor or script against these keys must update their patterns -- `kopiv2:tx:lock:leader` becomes `kopiv2:myseliasan:tx:lock:leader` (and the myidsan equivalent). During a rolling upgrade, an old and a new instance of the SAME app briefly use different key names and can therefore both consider themselves leader; for the duration of the rollout that means scheduled work may run twice rather than once, which the rollup cursor and the digest date-guard already tolerate. Restarting both instances of an app together avoids even that. Fixes (2) and (3) apply to standalone installs too and need no configuration: the false node-lost path was reachable on a single instance whenever a node reconnected (a node restart, or any dropped link), and the migration-lock defect only ever mattered where a distributed lock provider is configured. Fix (4) is a no-op under the default per-process lock provider, where the single instance is always leader. The event-bus topic rename has no upgrade concern at all: pub/sub channels hold no state, nothing is persisted under the old name, and only one app publishes or subscribes today.
